name: Which layers compute a later year?
notes:
Expect MLPs 9 and 10 to carry the largest effects, about a third of the gap each, then MLP 8, attention in layer 9 and MLP 11; attention in layers 5 to 8 adds a little, and layers 0 to 4 nothing.

The question: GPT-2 small continues “The war lasted from the year 1732 to the year 17” with a year after 32. Which layers compute that the end year comes after the start?

Published: Hanna et al. 2023, “How does GPT-2 compute greater-than?” (NeurIPS 2023), found by path patching, with the start year replaced by 01, that MLPs 8 to 11 compute it, MLPs 9 and 10 most, after attention heads 5.1, 5.5, 6.9, 7.10, 8.8, 8.11 and 9.1 bring the start year to the last token. On their prompts GPT-2 small's probability difference was 81.7%.

How it is measured: each clean prompt runs with one layer's attention or MLP output at the last token taken from the same prompt with the start year 01 (corrupt → clean), one at a time. The metric is the probability difference, P(a later year) − P(the start year or an earlier one), each summed over the two-digit years; an effect of 1 means the patch breaks the prediction as completely as the start year 01 does. The 96 prompt pairs come from Logogram's greater-than task, seed 0, with its three default templates (the paper used the first, “lasted”).

Measured on GPT-2 small at revision 607a30d: the probability difference is 0.82 (the paper's 81.7%), and −0.50 with the start year 01. MLP 9 (0.36) and MLP 10 (0.34) have the largest effects, then MLP 8 (0.20), attention in layer 9 (0.16) and MLP 11 (0.09), and attention in layers 7, 8, 5 and 6 (0.08 to 0.03); no attention or MLP output of layers 0 to 4 moves it by more than 0.004. This matches the paper. These are total effects of whole layers, not the paper's paths or single heads: to see heads 9.1, 8.11, 8.8 and 7.10, patch every head at the last token instead.
